overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to identify the litigation matter in the Aug 24, 2023 executive session notice and announcement, found the discussion itself proper, declined to nullify the vote, and ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Aug 24 executive session notice and open-session announcement described litigation only generally, without identifying the specific litigation matter to be discussed.
Complaint may be read as alleging the matters discussed in the Aug 24 executive session were inappropriate for executive session under Purpose 3.
allegations.key_passage: we find, after reviewing the minutes of the executive session, that the Committee permissibly discussed strategy with respect to pending litigation, and in particular, a potential settlement or resolution of the litigation.

allegations.summary: Complainant asked that the Aug 24 executive session vote be nullified as a remedy.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee has already taken sufficient remedial action, and therefore we decline to nullify the vote taken during the August 24 executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint also alleged ethics and elections law violations by Committee members in dealings with the teachers' union before the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We do not review, and offer no opinion on, whether the Committee may have violated other laws outside the Division's purview.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Caution that a future determination of a similar violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
